newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Moderate gain seen in Shui On Cons debut.
newsitem.headline: Moderate gain seen in Shui On Cons debut.

text.p: Shares of Shui On group unit Shui On Construction and Materials Ltd are expected to make moderate gains in their trading debut on Monday, analysts said on Friday.

"I think the share will gain good support in its debut due to its relatively bright business prospects, but a sharp rally is unlikely in view of its flotation response," said Ben Kwong, research director of Dharmala Securities.

Shui On Construction, a construction materials supplier and construction firm, offered 65 million shares at HK$9.30 per share. The 14.63 million shares for the general public were 14.03 times subscribed.
Of the flotation, 48.75 million shares were placed to professional investors and 1.62 million shares were for staff.

Analysts said the company's earnings potential was bright on anticipation of upcoming housing projects and underlying strong demand for construction materials from infrastructure and property developments.
"It is good timing for the listing because, overall, property and projects in Hong Kong and China are picking up," Kwong said.
Despite a promising long-term outlook, analysts said the company's relatively "steady but unexciting" earnings outlook is seen preventing the shares from rising too much in the short term.

"Generally, low profit margins and keen competition in the industry are the concerns," said a research manager at a local brokerage. "Short-term investors will find the shares unexciting in view of its rather steady earnings growth."
Shui On Construction said half of the HK$574.4 million net proceeds would be used to expand construction material operations in China, with the other half used for working capital.

The company supplies ready-mixed concrete, rock products, cement and ready-mixed mortar and other construction materials throughout Hong Kong and southern China. It also engages in the construction of public housing and institutional buildings.
